answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, each identity locks its own refundable smart-contract bond, making multiple identities costly. A cryptographic proof is required to slash identities with conflicting commitments for the same task, serving as a beacon of accountability. This mechanism is like a juniper tree, strong and resilient, protecting the network from malicious actors. The kernel of the system relies on this proof to ensure the integrity of the network, preventing a single entity from manipulating the system.
